Sandbox_ZomboidFixesB42_FastTransfers: Fast Item Transfers With Fast Timed Actions
Sandbox_ZomboidFixesB42_FastTransfers_to: In single player the Fast Timed Actions cheat makes moving items between containers quick. In multiplayer the server times every transfer itself and ignores the cheat, so an admin still waits the full time for each item. Tick this so the server moves items straight away for anyone who has Fast Timed Actions switched on and is allowed to use it. Transfers still play a short animation and still wait for the item to really arrive, so actions queued behind them, like eating out of a bag, keep working. Only works for staff with the cheat on; everyone else is not affected. If the server cannot make a quick transfer, the items are moved the normal way instead of not at all.
Sandbox_ZomboidFixesB42_AnimalGenderChan: The gender button in the animal info window only flips a flag on the admin's own screen. The animal keeps its model, cannot mate as its new gender, and changes back for other players or after the chunk reloads. Tick this to change the animal's type along with its gender, so a sow really becomes a boar and the other way round, keeping its name, age, stats and genes, and to make the change on the server so everyone sees it and it is saved. Works for animals on the ground, in hutches, in trailers and carried in the inventory. Needs the Animal Cheats capability.
Sandbox_ZomboidFixesB42_ForagingDebugFix: In multiplayer the foraging debug menu's icons exist only on the admin's screen: added icons cannot be picked up, moving every icon in a zone does nothing and refreshing a zone does not clear anything. Picking up any forage icon also never actually hands over the items in multiplayer. Tick this to register added icons on the server so they can be picked up, move and refresh icons on the server too, and have the server grant the items when an icon is picked up.
Sandbox_ZomboidFixesB42_ItemEditorSync_t: The admin item editor only saves changes for items in a player's own inventory, and even then often not for other players' items, so an edited item in a crate, a vehicle or on the floor goes back to how it was. Tick this to send every changed field to the server, which applies it to its own copy of the item and tells everyone, wherever the item is. Needs the Edit Item capability.
Sandbox_ZomboidFixesB42_FixDebugAddFluid: [BETA] Working Debug Add Fluid On World Objects

In multiplayer the debug Add Fluid option on a rain collector, barrel or other world object that holds fluid empties it instead of filling it, and nobody else sees the change. Tick this to fill the container to capacity with the chosen fluid on the server and send it to everyone. Feeding troughs and fluid containers on items already work and are not affected. Needs the Use Debug Context Menu capability.
Sandbox_ZomboidFixesB42_AdminTag_tooltip: Which admin panel cheats show the red admin tag above a staff member's head. Vanilla: the game's own rule, which forgets nine of the panel's cheats (fast move, unlimited ammo, know all recipes, brush tool, LootZed, loot log, animal cheats, animal extra values and always day), so a staff member with only those on shows no tag. Every Cheat: the tag shows while any cheat in the admin panel is on. Never: the tag is never shown.
Sandbox_ZomboidFixesB42_NoFastMoveFallDa: [BETA] No Fall Damage With Fast Move

Fast Move can carry a player over stairs faster than the game puts them on the steps, leaving them in the air until they drop, often to their death. Tick this so a player with Fast Move on glides down to the floor instead and takes no damage, without needing God Mode, which would also heal every wound and clear every moodle. Normal falls are not affected.
Sandbox_ZomboidFixesB42_DeleteNegativeWe: Items with a negative weight reduce a player's encumbrance and let them carry far more than they should. Tick this to delete any such item. Player inventories are checked every few seconds, and the floor, containers, corpses and vehicles around a player are checked as they come within reach. Each deletion is written to the server log.
Sandbox_ZomboidFixesB42_ClothingWearRewo: In single player, clothing and armor slowly lose condition from the zombie attacks they stop, and clothing torn down to nothing falls off. In multiplayer neither works: only attacks that get through reach the server, so armor with full protection never wears out, and clothing destroyed while worn drops only on your own screen and comes back on relog. Tick this to wear it down again: your own game rolls every zombie attack that lands on you, including from zombies another player's game is running, the way single player does, and sends each attack to the server, which wears your clothing with the game's own code (a hole costs the usual condition, hard armor loses a point now and then as set by its item script). Attacks add up on the server, so none can undo another. Destroyed clothing then falls off for everyone and stays destroyed, and the plain copy the game can leave on your character (a white scarf for a green one) is taken off. Wounds stay with the game as before. Untick it to go back to vanilla.
Sandbox_ZomboidFixesB42_RescueHutchAnima: Rescue Animals Lost In Hutch Nest Boxes

A hen laying an egg gives up her place inside the hutch while she sits in the nest box, so another bird can take it. If every place is taken when she finishes, the game deletes her instead of putting her back, and the player just sees a chicken that vanished. Tick this to catch her and put her back: into her own hutch, or one nearby, or a nest box if the coop really is full. Each rescue is written to the server log.
Sandbox_ZomboidFixesB42_HutchDirtSpeed_t: How fast hutches and their nest boxes get dirty, as a share of normal. 1 is vanilla and changes nothing; 0.25 is a quarter of the mess; 0 means they never get dirty. Nest boxes are the reason this exists: vanilla rolls for nest box dirt once per laying hen every frame, about eighty times as fast as the hutch floor beside it, so a busy coop goes from clean to filthy in a couple of minutes. Cleaning by hand is untouched, and time spent away from the coop is not affected.
Sandbox_ZomboidFixesB42_NoStairAutoVault: [BETA] No Auto Vault Over Stair Railings

Running into a low fence vaults it automatically, and the game never checks what is on the other side, so a jogging player who brushes the railing of a staircase, or the railing round a stairwell, goes over it and falls. Tick this to stop the automatic vault for railings on or beside stairs. Ordinary fences on flat ground still auto vault, and a stair railing can still be climbed on purpose by stopping and using the interact key.
Sandbox_ZomboidFixesB42_MultiplayerFastF: Puts the single player speed buttons and keys back on screen in multiplayer. Choosing a speed is a vote: the game only speeds up once every living player has chosen fast forward, and then at the slowest speed anyone chose. Timed actions such as reading or crafting speed up with it, including one already under way, and so do actions that work step by step (milking, shearing, reading, exercising, drinking, filling or emptying water and fuel, loading, swapping and racking guns and magazines), moving items between containers, cooking, and food heating up or cooling down, which on a server otherwise go at normal speed whatever the game speed. A player going back to normal speed takes back only their own vote: the game drops to normal speed, but everyone else's votes stay, so it speeds up again as soon as that player votes again. Finishing an action, or moving or driving, takes back that player's vote the same way (a player moving at fast forward speed breaks the anti-cheat's speed limit and gets kicked). A zombie close to anyone stops it and clears everyone's vote. Single player is not affected.
Sandbox_ZomboidFixesB42_AutoFastForwardA: Needs Multiplayer Fast Forward. Lets each player turn on auto fast forward for themselves: right-clicking a fast forward button turns it yellow, and right-clicking it again turns auto off. The choice is kept on the player's computer. While a button is yellow, a player who has been busy with timed actions (reading, crafting, building...) for Auto Fast Forward Delay seconds votes for that speed automatically, and finishing takes the vote back. Which actions do not count, and which must finish before the vote is cast, are set in Auto Fast Forward Ignored Actions and Auto Fast Forward Finish First Actions. The game still only speeds up while every player is voting, so it runs fast while everyone is busy with an action (or has voted by hand) and drops to normal while anyone is idle. Walking or driving takes the vote back until the player stands still at the action. Fishing never votes, including picking up the catch. Pressing Normal Speed, or a zombie close to anyone, stops it until that player's next action. Turn this off to hide the choice from everyone.
Sandbox_ZomboidFixesB42_AutoFastForwardD: Seconds a player must have been busy with timed actions before auto fast forward votes for them, so quick actions (eating a snack, equipping, opening a door) finish at normal speed and only long ones, or a long queue of actions, get sped up. Actions queued back to back count as one; a break of more than a second, or walking to the next action, starts the count again. 0 votes as soon as an action starts.
Sandbox_ZomboidFixesB42_AutoFastForwardI: Timed actions auto fast forward ignores: they never count as being busy, so doing one never votes, and ending one does not count as finishing an action. Write the actions' names as the game's Lua knows them (for example ISReadABook, as in the file names in the game's TimedActions folders), separated by commas, semicolons or spaces; capitals do not matter. Fishing stands for waiting for a bite with a fishing rod, which is not a timed action. By default: fishing, picking up the catch, and Tien's Weapon Inspection, which only holds the weapon up while its window is open.
Sandbox_ZomboidFixesB42_AutoFastForwardF: Auto Fast Forward Finish First Actions

Timed actions fast forward cannot speed up halfway through. When Auto Fast Forward Delay runs out during one of these, the vote waits until it is finished and is cast as the next action starts, instead of the game running fast while it still takes its normal time. Moving items (ISInventoryTransferAction) waits only for the item on its way, not the whole transfer: the vote is cast when that item arrives, and the next item waits the moment it takes the server to answer, then moves at the new speed. Looting a corpse can never be sped up, so it waits for the whole transfer. Write the names as for Auto Fast Forward Ignored Actions. By default: moving items, and grabbing items from the ground (ISGrabItemAction), which fast forward never speeds up. The speed buttons and keys are not affected by either list.
Sandbox_ZomboidFixesB42_GoMTooltipLineLe: Guns of Marz Tooltip Line Length

The game lists every weapon an attachment fits on one tooltip line, and a tooltip is only ever as narrow as its widest line, so once Guns of Marz has added thirty guns a scope or a laser throws a banner across the screen. Set the greatest number of characters a line may have and the list is rebuilt below the heading, wrapped, never splitting a name. Around 40 reads well; 0 leaves the tooltips as they are. The game writes its own heading before the wrapped list and it is left with nothing after it, because a tooltip can only be added to, never edited. Does nothing unless Guns of Marz is loaded.
Sandbox_ZomboidFixesB42_GoMMagazineToolt: When a Guns of Marz gun takes a different magazine, the server updates the gun, but the game's tooltip on your screen keeps naming and counting against an earlier magazine: the magazine type and capacity are not sent to you, and the name is remembered from the first time the tooltip was shown. So an M16 holding a 150 round drum reads 'STANAG 30Rds 5.56x45mm Magazine: 150+1 / 30'. Tick this to hide that line and show the magazine that is really in the gun, with its own capacity, instead. The corrected line goes at the end of the gun's stats, under the mod name, for every gun with a Guns of Marz magazine in it, because a tooltip can only be added to, never edited. Does nothing unless Guns of Marz is loaded.
Sandbox_ZomboidFixesB42_NISFShiftRange: Nick's Inventory Selection Fix Shift Range
Sandbox_ZomboidFixesB42_NISFShiftRange_t: Once Nick's Inventory Selection Fix stops selections from deselecting themselves, shift-clicking in an inventory or loot window can act like ctrl-clicking, adding one item at a time instead of selecting everything between. Tick this to make shift-click always select the whole range, including after a drag-box selection. Nick's mod ships its own attempt at this, which does not work, so this one runs ahead of it. Does nothing unless Nick's Inventory Selection Fix is loaded.
Sandbox_ZomboidFixesB42_GrabAmount_toolt: Right-clicking a stack of items in a container or on the floor only offers Grab one, Grab half and Grab all, and the same goes for item icons in search mode. Tick this to add Grab amount... after Grab one whenever there are at least three items: it asks how many to take (the last number you typed is filled in, Enter confirms) and then grabs exactly that many, walking and transferring like Grab all. Untick it to go back to vanilla.
Sandbox_ZomboidFixesB42_FirearmRadialNoB: [BETA] No Empty Slices In The Firearm Radial Menu

The radial menu that opens while the reload key is held keeps a fixed spot for every action (insert or eject magazine, load bullets into a magazine, rack) and leaves an empty slice where one cannot be done right now, for example Load Bullets into Magazine with every magazine full or no matching rounds. Tick this to leave those empty slices out, so the menu only shows what can be done. Slices other mods add are kept.
Sandbox_ZomboidFixesB42_TurboGameMultipl: Turbo Game's handheld console only half works on a server. Putting in a cartridge, taking it out and putting in a battery happen on the player's screen and not on the server, a console spawned from the item list can never take a cartridge, and the battery charge, the best scores and the boredom, unhappiness and stress a game changes all reset on relog. Tick this to have the server do all of it, so it sticks for everyone. A cartridge can then also go into an empty Turbo console, and the battery charge stays with the device it was in. Best scores and an unfinished Sudoku stay with the console they were played on too, so each console has its own, also in single player. The character also stays put while a game window is open, instead of walking around when the game's keys are pressed. Escape closes a game window. A game also cannot be played, and closes if it is open, when a zombie is near or it is too dark to read. Also works in single player. Does nothing unless Turbo Game is loaded.
Sandbox_ZomboidFixesB42_SewersClimbOut_t: With the Sewers mod on a server whose AntiCheatNoClip option is on (anything but disabled, 'log' included), climbing a ladder back up to the street does not work: the server takes the climb straight up through the floor for no-clip and puts the player back in the sewer, while climbing down is let through. Admins are put back without any log line; other players are logged, and kicked or banned if the option says so. Tick this so the server lets each climb out through: from the moment it grants the climb until it has the player on the street, normally a fraction of a second, AntiCheatNoClip is switched off, then set back to what it was. Nobody's no-clip is checked during that moment. Does nothing in single player, on a server with AntiCheatNoClip disabled, or unless the Sewers mod is loaded.
Sandbox_ZomboidFixesB42_AdminSpawnProtec: An admin brought back to a character that died, by reviving it on the server, loads in with the same fatal injuries and dies again straight away. Set a number of seconds and every admin who joins is fully restored the moment they arrive: every wound healed, infection cured, hunger, thirst, tiredness and the rest reset. They are then in god mode for that many seconds, after which it switches off again, unless they already had it on. 0 turns this off. Only admins, meaning roles that can turn on their own god mode, are affected, so relogging is never a free heal for players. Multiplayer only. Each restore is written to the server log.
Sandbox_ZomboidFixesB42_BodyStatsEditor_: The debug menu's Body panel only opens with the -debug launch option, only edits the admin's own character, and in multiplayer most of what it changes is undone by the server within a second. Tick this to give admins and moderators a Body button in the Player Stats window, an Edit your Body Stats button in the admin panel and a Body Stats entry in the scoreboard's right-click menu. It changes any online player's hunger, thirst, mood, health, infection, nutrition, weight, fitness and the other body stats on the server, so the changes stick and the player sees them. Needs the Can Modify Body Stats capability, never works on a player whose role ranks higher, and every change is written to the admin log. It also adds a Body part condition shortcut to the admin hotbar (new, not fully tested yet): it turns one condition on one body part on or off for any online player, such as a bite, a fracture, bleeding, a deep wound, glass shards, a lodged bullet, a burn, a wound infection or a muscle strain, with the same checks and log. Vanilla's health panel has the same toggles in its Cheat menu, but in multiplayer it sends them to the server with no permission check at all.
Sandbox_ZomboidFixesB42_ChopperControls_: Adds Send Chopper and Stop Chopper to the right-click Debug menu, and makes the debug menu's Add Chopper and Remove Chopper buttons do the same on a server. With vanilla's stop, the chopper event sends the chopper straight back within a minute or two for as long as the event lasts, and a late network packet can turn the chopper back on for some players. They then hear it hovering until they relog, and stopping it again does nothing, and the same can happen when the chopper event ends by itself. Stop Chopper ends today's chopper event if it is on, tells every player the chopper is gone, even when it already is, and repeats it over the next few seconds, so it also silences a chopper someone still hears after it left. With the Helicopter sandbox option on Sometimes or Often, the next chopper day is still planned as usual. The chopper still goes to a random online player, as in vanilla, and takes about a minute to fly in. Only for roles that may use the /chopper command, which are admins and moderators by default. Multiplayer only. Each use is written to the admin log.
Sandbox_ZomboidFixesB42_AdminHotbar_tool: Adds an Admin Hotbar button to the left sidebar, under the Admin button, for admins and moderators, and in single player when the game runs with the -debug launch option, where vanilla offers its own admin tools. It shows a floating bar of shortcuts to every admin tool: the Admin Powers, the admin panel windows, the right-click Tools and Debug menus (teleport, spawn vehicle, horde manager, make noise, thunder, fire), meta events, weather and climate, stories, animals, server messages and options, and player actions such as god mode, teleport, bring, add XP, kick and ban. A shortcut can carry settings (a target player, a location, an item, a vehicle, a saved climate or body preset) and then runs in one click; one without settings opens the vanilla window for it. Toggles such as god mode, rain or a climate preset turn green while on, amber while the server has not confirmed them yet. Every Item List, Spawn Vehicle, Horde Manager, Climate Control, Server Options, Teleport and Body window gets an Add to Hotbar button. Icons can be any image the game already has. Each admin keeps their own bar per server, and can bind a key to show it and a key to each of the first ten slots under Options, Key Bindings (Shift, Ctrl and Alt work). Every shortcut uses the game's own commands and needs the same role permissions as the vanilla tool it stands in for.
Sandbox_ZomboidFixesB42_AdminFullBright_: Adds Full Bright to the Admin Powers window and the admin hotbar, for roles that can use Always Day (the Climate Manager permission; single player: with the -debug launch option). Always Day only lights the outdoors, so rooms stay dark inside. Full Bright turns Always Day on and also lights every room around the admin, on every floor, with white light, as if all the lights were on. The light is only on the admin's own screen: nobody else sees it and nothing changes in the world. Like Always Day, lit squares let the admin read and let nearby zombies see the admin a little farther. Untick it to take Full Bright away.
Sandbox_ZomboidFixesB42_NoWalkOnSquarePi: [BETA] No Walking When Picking A Square

The debug Horde Manager's Pick New Square button and the Tile Picker use the same cursor as building, so clicking a square makes the character walk over to it first, sometimes a long way, unless the build cheat is on. Tick this so picking a square only selects it and the character stays where they are. Nothing is built or changed either way; only the walk is skipped.
Sandbox_ZomboidFixesB42_BooksStayRead_to: A skill book counts as read (the tick in the inventory, the Literature window) only when every page is recorded on the character, and in multiplayer the server's record is the one kept. The server never records the last pages when a book is finished: read with the instant timed actions cheat, the book is not recorded at all, and read normally it is often left a page short. It looks read until the next login and then shows as unread again. Tick this so a finished book is recorded as fully read on the server.
Sandbox_ZomboidFixesB42_ServerOptionsToo: The admin panel's Server Options window shows the description of the option under the mouse, but the game only takes that description away when the mouse moves to another spot in the same window. Leave the window quickly from an option, or close it, and the description stays on screen and follows the mouse around for the rest of the session. Tick this so it goes away when the mouse leaves the window and when the window closes, as it does in the other admin windows.
Sandbox_ZomboidFixesB42_VehicleBatteryDr: A mistake in the game's battery code counts every drain twice, so headlights, the radio, the lightbar and the siren left on with the engine off, and the heater while it runs, empty a car battery twice as fast as the game means them to. Tick this so each drains at its intended speed, which makes a battery last twice as long. Charging from a running engine was never affected and stays the same. Untick it to go back to the doubled drain.
Sandbox_ZomboidFixesB42_RemoveBushToolWe: Removing a bush or wall vines with a knife, machete, axe or other cutting tool is meant to tire the character, strain their arms and now and then wear the tool down, but the game loses track of the tool (in multiplayer the server never learns which one is in hand, in single player the event never fires), so none of it happens and every bush strains the back as if pulled out by hand. Tick this so each bush costs endurance, arm strain and a chance of tool wear, like chopping a tree does, and a tool that breaks is swapped for the best weapon left in the inventory. In multiplayer it also makes the inventory window refresh when the server swaps a broken tool or uses up building materials, which the game asks for under the wrong name. Untick it to go back to bushes never wearing the tool.
Sandbox_ZomboidFixesB42_WaterPlantOnce_t: In multiplayer, watering a plant is done twice, once by the player's game while the action runs and again by the server when it ends, so every plant gets twice the water it should and the watering can or bottle empties twice as fast. Tick this so the server alone waters the plant and takes the water from the can, once, when the action ends, never pouring more than the can still holds; cancelling part way waters the plant for the part already poured. Single player was never affected and stays the same. Untick it to go back to the doubled watering.
Sandbox_ZomboidFixesB42_CraftSoundsMP_to: In multiplayer, the sound of adding an ingredient to a soup, stew, salad or drink only plays on the cook's own game, so nobody nearby hears it. Tick this so the sound is passed on through the server to the players within 40 tiles, who hear it from the cook, starting and stopping with the action. Only the game's own ingredient sounds are passed on, and none for an invisible player. Crafting sounds (stirring, slicing, sawing...) are already shared by the game and are not touched. Single player is not affected. Untick it to go back to adding ingredients being silent for everyone else.
Sandbox_ZomboidFixesB42_ReloadAnimTiming: [BETA] Reloads Keep Pace With The Animation

In multiplayer the server cannot see the reload animation, so it puts rounds in, swaps magazines and finishes racking on timers of its own, and many of them do not match the animation: shotgun shells, revolver and lever action rounds go in slower than the hand moves, so the animation runs ahead of the count, bolt action rounds go in before the hand gets there, and racking a shotgun or swapping a rifle magazine ends half way through the motion. Tick this so the server times each of these by the length of the animation the player sees, at the same reload speed (skill, panic, ammo straps), as single player does. Some reloads get a little quicker and some a little slower, the way they already are in single player. Guns that Gunworks times itself are left alone. A delay of about the player's ping remains. Untick it to go back to the game's own timers.
Sandbox_ZomboidFixesB42_RepairLostEntiti: [BETA] Rain Collectors And Drying Racks Survive Crashes

When a server crashes, is killed instead of shut down, or is restored from a backup, rain collectors, wells, amphoras and drying racks can stop working (nothing to fill, drink from or dry on until they are picked up and placed again), and buckets, pots and other items that catch rain can turn into plain items that never hold water again, even once picked up. While nobody is near, the game keeps these objects in a separate file from the map, and a server saves the map and that file at different times, so a crash or a backup taken at the wrong moment loses them. Tick this so every broken one is rebuilt when its area loads: objects as newly built, items with an empty container, including broken items already in a player's inventory (checked when they join) or in a vehicle. Whatever a broken one held is lost. It also saves an area again right after such an object in it loads, so the map and the separate file stay in step and a crash no longer breaks them; that part is skipped while periodic backups (BackupsPeriod) are on in the server settings, because a save during a backup would hold up the whole server until the backup ends. Multiplayer only. Each repair is written to the server log.
Sandbox_ZomboidFixesB42_TransferResync_t: In multiplayer, when the server fails to move an item a player is picking up or moving, it never tells the player's game. The progress bar hangs for 10 to 20 seconds and the action then ends having done nothing. That leaves items on the floor that cannot be picked up and are gone after relogging (only that player's game still showed them), and items that vanished while being picked up and turn up in the inventory after relogging (the server moved them but the player's game was never told). Tick this so the player's game asks the server where the items really are whenever a transfer is refused, runs well past its end or times out. The server sends again anything the player cannot see, items that only the player's game showed are removed from its floor and containers, a transfer the server simply dropped is tried once more, and a transfer that did happen ends at once instead of hanging. Picking an item up off the ground is checked the same way. Items are never created, duplicated or moved by this, and nothing is taken out of the player's own inventory. Each repair is written to the server log. Multiplayer only; untick it to go back to vanilla.
Sandbox_ZomboidFixesB42_ItemDataFixes_to:
Fixes plain mistakes in vanilla item scripts. Items already loaded keep a copied value (weight, combat speed, wear chance) until they are next loaded, food keeps the nutrition it was created with, and loot that already spawned stays as it is. Untick it to go back to vanilla.
- Articulated Metal Shin Armor runs at 0.90 and Metal Shin Armor at 0.85 (they were the wrong way round).
- The right spiked metal and spiked scrap metal thigh armor can be moved to the left thigh.
- The plain left knee pad and the right gaiter spawn with their other half, like every other pair.
- The full bow tie weighs 0.1 instead of 1.0.
- Full chainmail sleeves slow the right arm more than the left, like every other pair (right 0.95, left 0.97).
- The left tire shoulder pad wears like the right one, and both protect their own upper arm instead of the torso.
- The sawn-off pump shotgun plays its start, stop and unloading sounds.
- The x2 scope fits the pump shotgun and the sawn-off pump shotgun.
- Leeks, jars of leeks and grapefruits get real nutrition values.
- Pie slices weigh 0.2 like cake slices, and a box of .44 Magnum rounds weighs 0.48 (its carton 4.8).
- A red mug of coffee gives back a mug, the Rangers baseball shirt covers the arms, the red baseball cap falls off like the other caps, and the seafood cooler makes the cooler sounds.
Sandbox_ZomboidFixesB42_RecipeFixes_tool:
Fixes recipes and repairs that lose, swap or refuse items. These edit the loaded recipes and repairs while the game runs. Untick it to go back to vanilla.
- Spiked articulated metal shoulder pads can be smelted into steel like the plain ones.
- The katana and the broken katana can be sharpened like every other long blade.
- Pasta cooked in a forged cooking pot gives back the forged pot instead of a normal one.
- Pasta and rice cooked in a copper saucepan can be split into 2 or 4 bowls, giving back the copper saucepan.
- Splitting a pot into clay bowls gives clay bowls of food (with mixed bowls, the last one put in decides), and beans, oatmeal, cereal or cake made with a clay bowl give the clay bowl back.
- Opening a pumpkin or sunflower seed packet gives all 25 seeds packing took, instead of 5.
- The sawn-off double barrel shotgun and the full one can repair each other and themselves (Aiming 2), like the pump shotguns.
